final_codebook.domain: Subtracting fractions and mixed numbers (including regrouping and simplification)

skills.name: Common denominator conversion
skills.definition: Find a least common denominator (LCD/LCM) and rewrite one or both fractions as equivalent fractions with that shared denominator before subtracting.
inclusion_criteria: The work explicitly determines an LCD/LCM of two denominators
The work scales numerator/denominator to create equivalent fractions with a common denominator prior to subtraction
exclusion_criteria: Denominators are already the same and no conversion is performed
The step only rewrites a whole number or mixed number into another form (tag S03 instead)

skills.name: Subtract like denominators
skills.definition: Compute the difference of two fractions that share a denominator by subtracting numerators and keeping the denominator (including results of 0 or negative fractional parts).
inclusion_criteria: Performs a/b − c/b = (a−c)/b after denominators match (whether originally or after S01/S03)
Subtracts fractional parts within mixed-number subtraction when denominators are the same
exclusion_criteria: Only finds an LCD and converts fractions without subtracting
Only borrows/regroups or simplifies/reduces without executing the numerator subtraction

skills.name: Rewrite number forms
skills.definition: Rewrite mixed numbers, improper fractions, or whole numbers into an equivalent form (e.g., mixed ↔ improper, or whole number as a fraction with a chosen denominator) to enable subtraction.
inclusion_criteria: Converts a mixed number to an improper fraction (or interprets a nonstandard mixed number like 1 4/3 as 1 + 4/3)
Rewrites a whole number as a fraction with a specified denominator (e.g., 4 = 12/3) or as a mixed number with a fractional part (e.g., 2 = 1 3/3)
exclusion_criteria: Only converts proper fractions to a common denominator (tag S01 instead)
Only borrows/regroups after a negative fractional part appears (tag S04 instead)

skills.name: Regroup and simplify
skills.definition: When fractional subtraction would be negative, borrow/regroup 1 whole into the fractional part (add b/b) and express the result in simplest form (reduce and/or convert to a mixed number/integer).
inclusion_criteria: Borrows 1 from the whole part and adds an equivalent 1 (b/b) to the fractional part to make subtraction possible (e.g., add 5/5, 10/10, 12/12, 24/24)
Reduces a resulting fraction to lowest terms and/or converts 0/b to 0 as part of finalizing the answer
Combines whole and fractional parts into a final mixed number or integer after regrouping/simplifying
exclusion_criteria: No regrouping is needed and no simplification/final-form step is shown
Only performs like-denominator subtraction without any borrowing or simplification beyond the subtraction itself (tag S02 instead)

decisions.details: Kept C01 as S01 (Common denominator conversion) with minor wording harmonization (LCD/LCM).
decisions.reasoning: Full 3/3 consensus and high diagnostic value as a distinct preparatory operation for fraction subtraction.

decisions.details: Renamed C02 to S02 (Subtract like denominators) while preserving the same concept and scope.
decisions.reasoning: All experts agree on the operation; the new name is shorter and matches the definition (like-denominator subtraction).

decisions.details: Refined C03 into S03 (Rewrite number forms) to explicitly cover mixed↔improper, whole-as-fraction with chosen denominator, and interpreting nonstandard mixed numbers.
decisions.reasoning: 3/3 consensus; refinement improves tagger reliability by clarifying the representational changes that belong here versus S01.

decisions.details: Refined C04 into S04 (Regroup and simplify) to include both borrowing/regrouping and final simplification/formatting as a single end-stage skill.
decisions.reasoning: 3/3 consensus on regrouping; A and C consistently include simplification/final form with regrouping, and bundling them maintains a clean 4-skill structure without creating an extra low-value skill.

summary: All aligned candidates had 3/3 expert consensus and mapped cleanly to four distinct operations in fraction/mixed-number subtraction. The final unified codebook keeps the four-skill structure, with minor renaming and refinements to improve clarity and consistent tagging, especially distinguishing denominator conversion (S01) from number-form rewriting (S03) and capturing regrouping plus final simplification (S04).
